Command: Do not rebuild an idolatrous city
Summary: One of the Deuteronomy 13 safeguards against idolatry: do not rebuild an idolatrous city. The chapter treats enticement to idolatry as a public danger to the whole community, not a private opinion.
Commandment: Do not rebuild an idolatrous city

Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: the destroyed city shall be an heap for ever, and shall not be built again (Deuteronomy 13:16) — the ruin itself stands as a witness against idolatry.
Function: This is classed as a moral law: it names a duty of character for Israel's life under the Law. One of the Deuteronomy 13 safeguards against idolatry: do not rebuild an idolatrous city. Scripture gives the reason: the destroyed city shall be an heap for ever, and shall not be built again. The evil it addressed was idolatry given a second home — the ruined city rebuilt and its worship resumed. It restrained that evil by leaving the ruin standing: the heap itself was the witness, and no one was to build on it again. These civil penalties belonged to ancient Israel's theocracy; the refusal to follow idolatrous leading endures.
